Business goal: Record async work intent durably in the same transaction as related domain state.
User outcome: Features can request background work without risking committed business state with a missing job.
Notes / constraints: Writes provider-neutral job/outbox metadata in PostgreSQL and does not expose BullMQ types to features.
Tenant context rule: tenant jobs require exactly one tenant context; root and platform-internal jobs declare scope explicitly
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; direct tenant enqueue outside approved feature capabilities
Authorization summary: Feature capabilities authorize business action before enqueue; no public enqueue API in v1.
Backend enforcement rule: Validate registered job type payload version scope idempotency key queue priority and payload safety before persistence.
Session / expiry behavior: No browser session behavior; actor stored only as audit attribution.
Request contract: Input includes jobType queueName/default payloadVersion payload idempotencyKey runAt priority executionScope tenantId and requester attribution.
Response contract: Returns jobId status queue priority payloadVersion and idempotency metadata.
Error contract: Validation unknown job type unsupported payload unsafe payload missing tenant duplicate idempotency persistence failure.
Cross-feature seams: Future consumers include notificationDelivery tenantAuth tenantAdmins imports exports campaigns and maintenance workflows.
Persistence impact: Creates durable job and outbox records plus idempotency metadata.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique idempotency key per job type where supplied; indexes on status queueName jobType runAt priority createdAt dispatch state.
Search / filter model: Future operator filters deferred; dispatcher polling by status runAt priority required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Provider boundary must allow BullMQ first and future SQS/RabbitMQ replacement.
Authorization enforcement layer: Feature service boundary plus registry validation; caller feature enforces user authz.
Audit requirement: Audit attribution persisted when supplied; future operator/manual enqueue audited.
Privacy / personal data impact: Payloads may reference personal data but must not contain secrets tokens credentials or authority grants.
Standards impact: High reliability security and anti-drift relevance.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when feature domain state and durable job request commit atomically without BullMQ imports.

Business goal: Publish committed durable job requests to BullMQ after transaction commit.
User outcome: Committed work eventually reaches Redis-backed execution even if the original web process crashes.
Notes / constraints: Dispatcher reads undispatched outbox rows and marks them dispatched only after provider acceptance.
Tenant context rule: no tenant decision by dispatcher; scope metadata is preserved
Authorization summary: Only internal dispatcher publishes outbox rows in v1.
Backend enforcement rule: Claim rows safely and publish idempotently where possible; do not inspect feature domain state.
Request contract: Worker config selects queues batch size poll interval and provider adapter.
Response contract: Dispatch logs/metadata include published skipped failed and next poll details.
Error contract: Provider unavailable timeout duplicate provider job stale lease persistence failure.
Cross-feature seams: BullMQ adapter hidden behind provider boundary.
Persistence impact: Updates outbox dispatch status providerJobId dispatch attempts lockedBy lockedUntil last error dispatchedAt.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on dispatch status runAt priority lockedUntil createdAt; provider job id unique where present.
Compatibility / migration notes: Dispatcher adapter can change for future providers without feature caller changes.
Authorization enforcement layer: Worker runtime and repository lease checks.
Audit requirement: Dispatch failures visible for future operator APIs.
Privacy / personal data impact: Do not log sensitive payloads or provider secrets.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when failed dispatch remains durable and retryable.

Business goal: Provide explicit registry of supported job types and handlers.
User outcome: Features add async handlers through governed registration rather than ad hoc queues.
Notes / constraints: Each job type declares owner feature payload versions schema scope queue priority retry policy and handler.
Tenant context rule: job type declares root tenant platform-internal or approved shared-cross-tenant scope
Explicitly denied roles: unregistered handlers; hidden discovery; direct provider use
Authorization summary: Only registered job types can be enqueued or executed.
Backend enforcement rule: Worker startup/registry validation rejects duplicate or invalid definitions.
Response contract: Deterministic registered job-type catalog for runtime validation.
Error contract: Duplicate job type missing schema missing handler invalid scope invalid queue invalid retry policy.
Cross-feature seams: Feature-owned handlers register through worker integration seam.
Persistence impact: No direct persistence unless registry snapshot is added later.
Search / filter model: Future operator APIs may read registry metadata.
Privacy / personal data impact: No payload data in registry definitions.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when only explicitly registered versioned jobs execute.

Business goal: Run registered handlers through workers with at-least-once semantics.
User outcome: Background work runs outside HTTP with durable attempts and crash recovery.
Notes / constraints: BullMQ owns live locks/stalled handling while the platform records durable execution state.
Tenant context rule: tenant handlers execute in exactly one tenant context and verify ownership
Authorization summary: Only worker runtime executes jobs; auth normally checked at enqueue time.
Backend enforcement rule: Validate job type version payload and scope before invoking handler; record attempt lifecycle.
Request contract: BullMQ job carries provider-neutral job id and metadata.
Response contract: Execution updates durable job and attempt state.
Error contract: Unknown job invalid payload canceled/stale job retryable/non-retryable handler error timeout persistence failure.
Cross-feature seams: Handlers call owning feature public seams only.
Persistence impact: Creates attempt records and updates job status/error summaries.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on job status jobType queue runAt attemptCount completedAt worker attempt fields.
Search / filter model: Future filters by status queue job type time.
Authorization enforcement layer: Worker validation plus handler domain validation.
Audit requirement: Attempt lifecycle and terminal failures durably visible.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when registered handlers run at least once with durable attempts and idempotency expectations.

Business goal: Apply consistent retry backoff jitter and terminal dead state.
User outcome: Transient failures recover without retry storms; exhausted jobs remain inspectable.
Notes / constraints: Default policy maxAttempts 5 initialDelay 30s exponential backoff jitter maxDelay 30m.
Tenant context rule: no tenant decision beyond persisted scope
Explicitly denied roles: public callers; tenant retry controls in v1
Authorization summary: Retry is automatic in v1; manual retry deferred.
Backend enforcement rule: Record every attempt and move exhausted jobs to dead state without deleting history.
Request contract: Retry policy from registry or constrained enqueue override.
Response contract: Durable nextRunAt attempt count and dead reason.
Error contract: Invalid retry policy retryable failure non-retryable failure exhausted attempts provider scheduling failure.
Persistence impact: Updates attempts nextRunAt status deadLetterReason terminal timestamps.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index on status nextRunAt jobType dead state.
Search / filter model: Future filters by dead retryable delayed jobs.
Compatibility / migration notes: Model should translate to future providers where possible.
Audit requirement: Dead-letter and future manual actions audit-visible.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when retries back off with jitter and exhausted jobs preserve history.

Business goal: Require small versioned validated JSON payloads.
User outcome: Queued work remains safe to retry inspect and migrate.
Notes / constraints: Payloads carry stable references by default; durable snapshots require design exception.
Tenant context rule: tenant payloads include exactly one tenant id when required
Authorization summary: Enqueue and execution require supported payload version and schema-valid data.
Backend enforcement rule: Reject unsafe fields oversized data and unsupported versions.
Response contract: Validated payload metadata or validation error.
Error contract: Unsupported version invalid schema oversized payload forbidden secret/token missing stable reference.
Persistence impact: Persist payload JSON and safe metadata with redacted future display.
Indexes / uniqueness: Do not index arbitrary JSON; important searchable fields are scalar metadata.
Compatibility / migration notes: Versioning allows old queued jobs to run after handler evolution.
Authorization enforcement layer: Registry schema validation plus common safety checks.
Audit requirement: Unsafe payload rejection visible in tests/logs.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when secret-bearing or authority-bearing payloads are rejected.

Business goal: Declare and enforce root tenant platform-internal or approved cross-tenant job scope.
User outcome: Async execution cannot bypass tenant isolation or replay stale request authority.
Notes / constraints: Jobs carry stable context not authority; requester actor is audit attribution only.
Tenant context rule: tenant jobs require exactly one tenant context
Authorization summary: Authorization normally checked at enqueue; execution uses constrained system authority and domain-state validation.
Backend enforcement rule: Registry and enqueue validation require scope; tenant handlers verify object ownership.
Request contract: Job type declares execution scope; enqueue includes tenantId when required.
Response contract: Persisted scope metadata and rejections for invalid context.
Error contract: Missing/ambiguous tenant unapproved cross-tenant token payload object-tenant mismatch.
Cross-feature seams: Handlers consume approved feature seams only.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index on executionScope tenantId jobType related metadata.
Compatibility / migration notes: Preserves tenant boundary defaults as async grows.
Authorization enforcement layer: Registry/enqueue validation and handler domain checks.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when jobs cannot smuggle authority and tenant handlers prove ownership.

Business goal: Define queue priority and concurrency defaults.
User outcome: Bulk work does not block routine or critical work.
Notes / constraints: Initial queues critical default bulk maintenance; priority sorts within queue; chunking prevents monopolies.
Authorization summary: Feature code may use registered defaults but cannot boost into critical arbitrarily.
Backend enforcement rule: Registry constrains queue/priority; worker honors queue concurrency.
Request contract: Job definition includes defaultQueue defaultPriority concurrency/rate-limit hints.
Error contract: Invalid queue unknown priority unauthorized critical invalid concurrency.
Cross-feature seams: BullMQ queues hidden behind platform queue names.
Persistence impact: Persists effective queueName priority and maybe config snapshot.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index queueName priority runAt status createdAt.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when queue-level concurrency and job-type defaults isolate workloads.

Business goal: Persist metadata for later job/queue/worker inspection.
User outcome: Troubleshooting can be added later without redesigning execution.
Notes / constraints: Operator APIs/UI are deferred but schema preserves job id queue type payload version redacted metadata status priority attempts timestamps worker id errors related refs idempotency dead state.
Tenant context rule: tenant metadata protected by future root/operator access
Authorization summary: No operator read API in v1; future APIs root-authorized and audited.
Backend enforcement rule: Persist safe metadata and redact full payload display.
Client-side permission behavior: Future UI hides operations without grants.
Request contract: Deferred queries by queue type status tenant related entity dead state time.
Response contract: Deferred safe responses with attempts and redacted payload.
Error contract: Future validation authz not-found stale unsafe disclosure errors.
Cross-feature seams: Feature progress APIs separate from generic job APIs.
Persistence impact: Creates durable job/attempt metadata for future read/retry/cancel/health surfaces.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index status queueName jobType tenantId relatedEntity timestamps dead state.
Search / filter model: Future search scalar columns not raw payload JSON.
Session / auth dependency: Future root session; no v1 session.
Compatibility / migration notes: Deferred APIs should not redesign execution.
Authentication requirement: No v1 external auth; future root auth.
Authorization enforcement layer: Future root authz plus redaction guards.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when v1 runs without APIs while preserving future troubleshooting metadata.

Business goal: Preserve future root-operator retry cancel and queue-management semantics.
User outcome: Safe operator controls can be added later when operational failures justify them.
Notes / constraints: Manual controls deferred; state model distinguishes retryable failed dead canceled running delayed succeeded.
Tenant context rule: no tenant operator action in v1
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors unauthenticated callers root users without future grants
Authorization summary: Future controls require root authz and audit; no controls in v1.
Frontend visibility rule: Future UI controls only when allowed and safe.
Backend enforcement rule: V1 state machine must preserve terminal statuses and attempt history.
Request contract: Future requests include reason state precondition filters max batch size.
Response contract: Future responses include state audit id summary.
Error contract: Future invalid state stale precondition unauthorized unsafe retry partial failure.
Cross-feature seams: Feature-owned domain state may need coordinated hooks.
Persistence impact: V1 stores statuses/attempts for future manual transitions.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes for terminal/dead-letter queries where cheap.
Search / filter model: Future filters by status type queue related entity.
Compatibility / migration notes: Manual actions need later ADR/PRD update if cross-cutting.
Authorization enforcement layer: Future root authz and state-transition validation.
Audit requirement: Future actions audited with actor reason affected jobs.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when controls are deferred but feasible.

Business goal: Define durable item-level progress pattern for batch features.
User outcome: Large workflows can resume and expose progress/ETA.
Notes / constraints: Queue tracks generic job state; user progress belongs to feature-owned records such as recipients rows or chunks.
Capability boundary (root - tenant - sha: tenant or root depending on feature
Tenant context rule: batch item state follows owning feature scope
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; unapproved cross-tenant batch work
Authorization summary: Owning feature authorizes batch creation; foundation gives guidance/execution primitives.
Frontend visibility rule: Future feature UI uses feature APIs not generic jobs.
Backend enforcement rule: Handlers claim chunks durably and mark item states pending queued processing succeeded failed dead canceled.
Frontend required?: No per foundation; yes in consuming features
Request contract: Feature-owned progress responses use domain terms.
Feature seam(s): Consuming features own item records/progress APIs.
Cross-feature seams: No generic batch item table in v1.
Persistence impact: No for foundation; yes for consumers
Migration required?: Consumer indexes on batch id status claimedUntil timestamps identity.
Indexes / uniqueness: No raw payload search for progress.
Search / filter model: Feature-owned progress filters by batch status and timestamps.
Compatibility / migration notes: Design gate not generic batch engine.
Authorization enforcement layer: Owning feature authz plus job scope checks.
Audit requirement: Batch progress/manual retries audit-visible where sensitive.
Privacy / personal data impact: Potentially high depending on item data.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when batch features model per-item progress and interrupted workers resume from DB state.

Business goal: Give workers stable identity and graceful shutdown.
User outcome: Deploys/restarts do not create ambiguous job history or unnecessary duplicate work.
Notes / constraints: Worker identity includes host/pid/boot id; shutdown handles SIGTERM/SIGINT and bounded drain.
Backend enforcement rule: Record worker id on attempts and shut down cleanly.
Request contract: Runtime config includes workerId drain timeout queue list concurrency.
Response contract: Logs/future metadata show worker identity and shutdown outcome.
Error contract: Shutdown timeout provider close failure stalled job persistence failure.
Cross-feature seams: BullMQ lock/stalled mechanics hidden behind adapter.
Persistence impact: Attempt records store workerId and timestamps; heartbeat table deferred.
Compatibility / migration notes: Provider replacement preserves worker identity semantics.
Audit requirement: Worker lifecycle may be logged/audited later.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when workers record identity and shutdown without losing durable state.

Business goal: Support delayed jobs while deferring recurring scheduling toolkit.
User outcome: Immediate and simple delayed work can run now without designing cron workflows.
Notes / constraints: V1 supports runAt/delay; recurring jobs cron calendars UI deferred.
Explicitly denied roles: public schedule mutation; hidden recurring jobs
Authorization summary: Only internal seam may use runAt; recurring schedules require later PRD.
Backend enforcement rule: Accept optional runAt; no recurring schedule definitions in v1.
Request contract: Optional runAt timestamp; no cron contract.
Error contract: Invalid runAt bounds unsupported recurring schedule provider delay error.
Cross-feature seams: Future scheduling toolkit builds on enqueue seam.
Persistence impact: Stores runAt/status; no schedule table in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Do not mistake delayed jobs for scheduling toolkit.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when delayed one-off jobs work and recurring scheduling is deferred.

Business goal: Preserve first-consumer path for notificationDelivery retry.
User outcome: Email delivery can later use queue foundation through outboundEmailId.
Notes / constraints: Adoption is deferred; planning aligns with notificationDelivery durable email/attempt model.
Tenant context rule: tenant metadata may be attached but not broad tenant authority
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; direct public email jobs
Authorization summary: Future adoption calls jobProcessing through approved seams; this slice does not change notificationDelivery.
Backend enforcement rule: Later handler loads outboundEmailId and creates attempts idempotently.
Frontend route: Future notificationDelivery APIs unchanged unless retry APIs added
Frontend states: Root session for operator routes where applicable
Route(s): Future internal worker handler not public route.
Response contract: Returns generic job status and notificationDelivery delivery status.
Error contract: Provider retryable/non-retryable unsafe resend duplicate missing outboundEmail errors.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes notificationDelivery public seam and jobProcessing seam.
Persistence impact: No change in planning slice; later adoption may add records.
Indexes / uniqueness: Existing notification attempt indexes plus jobProcessing indexes.
Session / auth dependency: Existing root session for operator email routes.
Authorization enforcement layer: Existing route authz plus worker validation.
